Duties:

•	Select, inspect and prepare quality ingredients to ensure consistency and high standards of food quality.
•	Supervise and coordinate kitchen operations to ensure the timely preparation and service of meals.
•	Monitor food preparation and presentation to maintain quality, portion control and consistency.
•	Estimate food requirements, place stock orders, monitor inventory levels and conduct regular stocktakes to minimise waste and ensure adequate supplies.

•	Demonstrated experience in planning menus and developing new dishes and seasonal menu items.
•	Ability to estimate food and labour costs, order supplies and maintain appropriate stock levels.
•	Strong knowledge of food preparation, cooking techniques, presentation and quality control.
•	Proven ability to supervise, train and mentor kitchen staff and contribute to the efficient operation of the kitchen.

Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network 

Angaston

AHP2 $94,997 - $110,052 (adjusted to hours worked)

Full Time, Ongoing - start Oct 2026 

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

In this role, the Allied Health Professional will use clinical experience and growing professional knowledge to deliver a range of integrated mental health services. Care is tailored to the needs of consumers and the local community. Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will provide person-centred support through preventative, early intervention and therapeutic approaches. This includes individual, family and group work. You will manage a varied caseload and support recovery and community connection. 

Working with reduced clinical direction, you will also support and guide less experienced staff and students. You will take part in ongoing professional development and reflective practice. Strong communication and teamwork are essential. You will help improve service quality, support integration across services, and contribute to culturally safe, responsive care within the Local Health Network.

WHO ARE WE? 

The Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network offers opportunities across our sites, from Kangaroo Island to Eudunda, wrapping all the way around our metropolitan areas. We pride ourselves on providing exceptional care to all our consumers, residents, their families, and community. Our mission is to ensure that you always receive the best quality, safe, consistent, collaborative care and always with kindness. We do this by maintaining exceptional levels of care at all times supported by systems and processes that assure us of quality and safety of our staff and those we serve. 

WHERE AND HOW YOU WILL WORK 

Located in the heart of the Barossa Valley, Angaston offers a relaxed country lifestyle surrounded by world-renowned wineries, local produce, and a strong sense of community. Just over an hour from Adelaide, it combines rural charm with convenient access to metropolitan services, making it an ideal location for work-life balance. 

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

Are you committed to delivering high-quality care?

Do you have a strong motivation to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team and build strong partnerships with families, community services and external stakeholders?

Are you driven to continuously develop clinical skills and apply evidence-based practice in increasingly complex and diverse service settings?

Do you aim to achieve a culturally safe practice, with a genuine interest in supporting rural, Aboriginal and diverse communities? 

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will. 

Deliver comprehensive, evidence-based occupational therapy- mental health care, applying contemporary practice and local service knowledge to support consumers, carers, and the broader multidisciplinary team.

Manage a complex and varied caseload with increasing autonomy, applying clinical judgement and evidence-based practice to assessment, intervention, health promotion and early intervention activities.

Collaborate within a multidisciplinary team and with external partners to provide coordinated, culturally safe care, particularly for rural, Aboriginal and diverse communities.

Contribute to clinical leadership, supervision and workforce development by supporting junior staff, allied health assistants and students, while actively engaging in ongoing professional development and reflective practice.

Support service quality and sustainability through effective documentation, data reporting, and participation in continuous improvement activities. 

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways: 

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information 

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities.

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families. 

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS? 

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following: 

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy. Further information is in the application for to help guide you.

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. We continually look for ways to support and promote diversity and flexible ways of working so please let us know what interests you.

NEED TO RELOCATE?

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Project Engineer to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Project Engineer, you will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering engineering projects across mining, oil and gas, and industrial sectors. You will work closely with project managers, clients, engineers, supervisors, and site personnel to ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget, and in accordance with contractual and engineering requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Plan, coordinate, and manage engineering projects from commencement through to completion.
•	Review engineering drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation.
•	Prepare project schedules, work programs, budgets, cost estimates, and resource plans.
•	Coordinate engineering, fabrication, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities.
•	Monitor project progress and ensure milestones, budgets, and quality standards are achieved.
•	Liaise with clients, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, and internal project teams.
•	Identify technical issues and provide practical engineering solutions to minimise project risks.
•	Ensure compliance with Australian Standards, engineering specifications, contractual obligations, and company procedures.
•	Prepare technical reports, progress reports, project documentation, and engineering correspondence.
•	Assist with tender preparation, cost planning, and contract administration.
•	Conduct site inspections and support project delivery teams to ensure safe and efficient execution of works.
•	Promote and maintain compliance with workplace health, safety, environmental, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Civil, Structural, or related discipline).
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as a Project Engineer or in a similar engineering role.
•	Experience delivering mining, industrial, fabrication, maintenance, shutdown, or construction projects.
•	Strong knowledge of project planning, engineering principles, contract administration, and project delivery.
•	Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and technical documentation.
•	Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and organisational skills.
•	Strong communication and stakeholder management abilities.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced project environment.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and project management software.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $100,000 – $140,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing professional development and career progression.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

Store/Retail Manager

Coober Pedy Cellar Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced and reliable Retail Manager to oversee the day-to-day management of its liquor retail operations.

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing store operations, improving customer service standards, supporting sales growth, overseeing stock selection, and ensuring the business operates efficiently and in accordance with applicable liquor licensing requirements.

Location: Coober Pedy, South Australia
Employment Type: Full-time, Permanent and Ongoing
Annual Remuneration: $80,000 to $86,000 p.a. plus super.


Key responsibilities

As the Retail Manager, you will be responsible for:

•	Managing the day-to-day store operations. 
•	Developing retail objectives and preparing and implementing operating plans, marketing strategies, advertising initiatives, and store improvement plans
•	Determining the products and brands to be stocked by reviewing product trends, sales trends, and customer preferences
•	Setting prices for merchandise to achieve required profit margins while ensuring compliance with liquor restrictions
•	Achieve financial targets and develop budgets.
•	Selecting suppliers and vendors and placing stock orders within budget
•	Overseeing promotional activities and ensuring effective presentation of products
•	Setting customer service objectives and ensuring high service standards are maintained
•	Managing team.
•	Ensuring the store operates safely, efficiently, and in compliance with relevant laws, policies, and procedures


To be considered for this role, applicants should have:

•	At least 3 years of full time or part time equivalent experience in retail management, preferably within liquor retail or a similar customer-facing retail environment
•	A relevant diploma or higher qualification or at least 3 years of relevant experience in lieu of a qualification
•	Strong knowledge of retail operations, stock control, pricing, sales, and customer service
•	Ability to analyse sales trends and customer preferences
•	Strong communication, leadership, and organisational skills
•	Ability to manage suppliers, budgets, promotions, and day-to-day store operations
•	Understanding of liquor retail compliance requirements
•	Appropriate rights to work in Australia

This is a suitable opportunity for a motivated Retail Manager who can take responsibility for store performance, staff coordination, customer service, and operational standards.
Applications from suitably qualified candidates are encouraged.


How to apply:

Applications open on 24 July 2026 and close on 23 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.
